items.title: For a smooth affine morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres the functor of flatness in dimensions at least d is a finite disjoint union of the functors of fibrewise freeness of a given rank
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism X -> S of affine schemes with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension d and a quasi-coherent module F of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that the functor F_d defined by flatness in dimensions at least d is the disjoint union of the functors H_p of fibrewise freeness of rank p, for p running from 0 to some c (statement lines 7777-7786). The proof first bounds the ranks: since X is affine and F is of finite presentation, F is generated by c elements, so the dimension of F_x tensor kappa(x) never exceeds c and hence H_p is empty for p greater than c, which also shows the inclusion of the disjoint union into F_d (proof lines 7789-7794). The content is then identified precisely: for a base change F_T flat in dimensions at least d over T and a point t of T, one must show that F_T is free of some rank r on an open neighbourhood of the generic point of the fibre X_t, because then H_r contains the image of that neighbourhood, which is an open neighbourhood of t; this existence is quoted from the flat-and-free-at-a-point-of-the-fibre lemma (proof lines 7795-7802). Identifying the two functors through the generic point of the fibre is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
